title: Scope functions: let, run, with, apply and also

videos.script: Five functions with short names, and they all do the same thing. They run a block of code with an object in hand. That is why everybody mixes them up. {{grid}} This lesson sorts them with two questions. Inside the block, is the object called it, or this? And what comes back: the object, or the block's result? Two answers each, four boxes, five names. {{let}} Let, behind a safe call, for a value that might be missing. {{apply}} Apply, for setting an object up and handing it on. {{also}} Also, for doing something on the way past, without changing what flows through. {{run}} Run and with, for computing a result with the object's members close at hand. {{nested}} Then the warning. Nest two of them, and this means the innermost object, and a reader has to work out every call by hand. Sometimes the clearest scope function is none.
